attributes.name: Company Name
attributes.description: Legal or operating name of the competitor entity.

attributes.name: Company Description
attributes.description: Brief narrative of what the company does and its core business model in the storage/cleantech space.

attributes.name: Year Founded
attributes.description: Year the company was established.

attributes.name: HQ Location
attributes.description: Primary headquarters city and state.

attributes.name: Employee Count
attributes.description: Approximate number of full-time employees.

attributes.name: Revenue Estimate
attributes.description: Estimated annual revenue or AUM in development pipeline (USD).

attributes.name: Funding / Capital Backing
attributes.description: Total equity raised, credit facility size, or parent company backing — relevant to development pipeline capacity.

attributes.name: Primary Business Model
attributes.description: Core model: develop-and-sell, develop-own-operate, EPC contractor, IPP, technology provider, or hybrid.

attributes.name: NY Market Presence
attributes.description: Active presence in New York State storage market — number of deployed or in-development NY projects.

attributes.name: NY Deployed / Pipeline MW
attributes.description: Estimated megawatts of BESS capacity deployed or in active NY pipeline.

attributes.name: Target Buyer / Off-taker
attributes.description: Primary customer or off-taker type: IPP, utility, municipality, C&I end-user, or own balance sheet.

attributes.name: Project Scale Focus (MW)
attributes.description: Typical project size range pursued — distributed (<10 MW), mid-scale (10–100 MW), or utility-scale (>100 MW).

attributes.name: Standalone vs. Solar+Storage Hybrid
attributes.description: Whether competitor pursues standalone BESS, solar+storage hybrid, or both configurations.

attributes.name: NYISO Market Participation
attributes.description: Depth of NYISO engagement: capacity market (UCAP), ancillary services (regulation, spinning reserves), energy arbitrage, or none.

attributes.name: NY Incentive Program Access
attributes.description: Demonstrated access to NY-specific incentive programs: NYSERDA TCES, Consolidated Edison BQDM, NY-SUN, or Con Edison/National Grid programs.

attributes.name: ITC / Tax Credit Utilization
attributes.description: Approach to monetizing federal Investment Tax Credit (ITC) and IRA adders — own tax appetite, tax equity partnership, transferability.

attributes.name: NY Interconnection Queue Experience
attributes.description: Track record navigating NYISO or Con Edison/NYSEG distribution interconnection queues for storage projects.

attributes.name: NY Permitting & Siting Capability
attributes.description: In-house or proven external capability for Article 10/Article 94 or local permitting processes in NY.

attributes.name: Development Pipeline Capacity
attributes.description: Estimated number of projects or MW in active development pipeline nationally and in NY.

attributes.name: Site Origination Model
attributes.description: How competitor sources project sites: proprietary prospecting, broker relationships, landowner outreach, utility partnerships.

attributes.name: Project Model Replicability
attributes.description: Degree to which competitor has a standardized, repeatable project template (site criteria, configuration, contract structure) enabling multi-site rollout.

attributes.name: BESS OEM / Technology Partnerships
attributes.description: Key battery technology suppliers or OEM partners (e.g., Tesla Megapack, Fluence, BYD, CATL, LG, Powin) and exclusivity or preferred terms.

attributes.name: EPC / Construction Delivery Model
attributes.description: Whether competitor self-performs EPC, uses a captive EPC subsidiary, or procures from third-party contractors.

attributes.name: IPP Buyer Relationships
attributes.description: Established relationships with IPP acquirers active in NY (e.g., AES, Orion, LS Power, Eolian, Spearmint, Key Capture) as repeat buyers.

attributes.name: Develop-and-Sell Transaction Track Record
attributes.description: Number and MW of storage development projects successfully sold to IPPs or third-party acquirers.

attributes.name: Demonstrated Returns / IRR Viability
attributes.description: Evidence (public, inferred, or disclosed) that competitor achieves acceptable project-level or developer returns in distributed NY BESS context.

attributes.name: Revenue Stack Optimization
attributes.description: Sophistication in stacking and optimizing multiple NY revenue streams: capacity, ancillary services, energy arbitrage, incentives, demand charge reduction.

attributes.name: Competitive Moat / Differentiation
attributes.description: Primary source of durable advantage: pipeline depth, policy relationships, proprietary software, balance sheet, brand, technology exclusivity.

attributes.name: Geographic Focus
attributes.description: Primary state or regional markets of activity — NY-focused, Northeast, national, or global.

attributes.name: Solar + Storage Integration Capability
attributes.description: Whether competitor has proven capability to co-develop and co-optimize solar PV and BESS on shared sites, including shared interconnection.

rationale: The NY distributed BESS developer market is moderately concentrated: a small tier of well-capitalized pure-play storage developers (Key Capture, Eolian, Spearmint, Convergent) have established meaningful NY pipelines, while a secondary tier of solar-storage hybrid developers, IPP subsidiaries, and regional entrants compete for the same distributed-scale sites and NYISO market access. The 8–16 range is appropriate because: (1) the distributed sub-10 MW class narrows the field relative to utility-scale — most national storage developers focus above this threshold; (2) NY's unique regulatory complexity (NYISO, NYSERDA, Article 94, Con Edison territory rules) creates meaningful barriers that filter out less-sophisticated entrants; (3) NEE's develop-and-sell model means the matrix should include both direct development competitors and the IPP buyers who are also sometimes vertical developers, creating a bounded but meaningful competitive set. Fewer than 8 would miss important regional players; more than 16 would dilute signal with peripheral participants who are not true analogs to NEE's specific configuration and buyer target.
